summary: Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and indology. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Peking University, Academia Sinica (~1950–1977 as Professor), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995 as Professor).
Xiaoting Wei specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. Wei completed an MA at the National University of Singapore (~2002–2004) under the supervision of Cheng-Mei Ku.

Xinchuan Huang worked in indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Peking University (~1954–1958) and served as a researcher (研究員) at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–2021).

Xinru Liu works in indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), she held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1985–1998) and The College of New Jersey (~1999–2021).

Xiuzhi Zeng specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zeng completed an MA at Nanhua University (~2003–2006) under supervisor Meihua Chen, with Chaocheng Lin and Chien-hsing Ho serving on the committee in ~2005.

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005–2008) under Xueyu and was appointed associate professor (副教授) at Renmin University of China in ~2011.

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, indology, and tibetology. Li became a Research Associate at China Tibetology Research Center in ~2006, studied under Shoryu Katsura in 2011, and was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011–2013).

Y. Karunadasa worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under W. S. Karunaratne and completed doctoral research at SOAS/University of London under David Friedman (~1960–1963). He later served at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and HKU.

Yael Bentor specializes in tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University under Gregory Schopen and others, also training with Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche. In ~1993, she began teaching at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Zhou studied at the National University of Singapore (~2007–2012), completing a PhD supervised by Yuet Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An works in Buddhist studies. An studied under Hojin and earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (~1993–1998) under the supervision of Richard Gombrich.
Yangdon Dhondup specializes in tibetology. She completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (~1999–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.

Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. Chen studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun and earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (~2009–2012) under Yongdong Shi, with Cheding and Yi-hsun Huang on the committee.
Yao Wang worked in tibetology and sinology. Wang studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna (~1990–1992).
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of California (~1991–1997) and became Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University in ~1997.

Yaping Dou works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Dou completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006–2010) under doctoral supervisor Xueyu, with Lai Chi-tim and Tianxiang Ma on the committee.

Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes under traditional teachers, and at the University of Virginia (~2001–2007). He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~2007–2008) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~2008).

Yaroslav Vassilkov works in indology. He studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1962–1967) and later held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1967) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1995, ~2001).

Yasuaki Nara worked in Buddhist studies and indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958) under Kogen Mizuno, and held posts at Komazawa University (1960–1961) and as director (所長) at the Soto Zen Comprehensive Research Center.

Yasuhiko Nagano works in tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1978) and held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1982–2011 as Professor) and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1989–2011).
